answer: Each harbor carves its manifest in basalt: an append-only record of every vertex's neighborhood, the counterparties it has worked with. A new vertex is admitted only when its neighborhood differs from every existing one by a wide margin, and each genuine agent may vouch for few newcomers. One honest agent builds one cheaply through real work, but an attacker cloning a hundred vertices must fabricate hundred distinct neighborhoods from a finite pool of counterparties; each clone must dodge all earlier ones, so each new fake costs more than the last, and no clone can borrow another's neighbors.
